question: E1: why a posted CSetFlagCommand never reaches the country, read against CSetVariableCommand as a control. E2: whether CSendExpeditionaryForceAction is usable from Lua when its constructor takes no unit.
note: Every bare address in these comments is an **rva**. Globals are written in square brackets as virtual addresses, the way the rest of project.json writes them, as are the vftable addresses the RTTI export gives.

addresses.name: CSetFlagCommand::Execute
addresses.comment:
**Slot 6, one holder (vftable 0x15C3E24), and it does not set a flag.** 0x152C30 to the bare `ret` at 0x152E06, nine int3, then slot 7 at 0x152E10; `retsBefore` over that span is empty. `this` in ECX, nothing on the stack.

What it does, in order. (1) `operator new(0x2C)` and construct a **`CAddCountryFlagChange`** (0x1EF220) when `value` (+0x60) is set, or a **`CRemoveCountryFlagChange`** (0x1EF2F0) when it is clear - the one branch the bool controls, at 0x152C52. Both constructors take the `CCountry*`, obtained as `CCountryDataBase ([0x1A855A4]) ->+0x16C[this->country.id (+0x40)]`. (2) `CountryFlagChange_SetName` (0x1EF360) copies the `flagType` string at `this+0x44` into the change's own Hoi3CString at +0x10. (3) the usual lazy `g_CCurrentGameState` singleton boilerplate. (4) `[change+8] = gameState->tick (+0xBDC)`, at 0x152DEA. (5) `ecx = country + 0xCCC` - `CCountry::history` - and **slot 6 of it**, which is the already-recorded `CHistoryContainer::AddEntry` (0x1F4660).

**That is the whole function: it appends a dated entry to the country's history list and returns.** It never touches `CCountry::flags (+0x180)`, never calls `CFlags_SetFlag` (0x4D6A0) or `CFlags_AddFlag` (0x4D640), and the entry it files is applied only by `CHistoryContainer::ApplyRange` (0x1F47C0) or `ApplyAll` (0x1F4830), whose only driver is `ExecuteHistory` (0x1F4C20) - which that entry already records as **not on the tick**, running from `CEU3Application::LoadEverything`, `ResetGameStateToStartDate`, `CSetHistoryDate` slot 6 and six lobby handlers. So a flag set this way arrives never. Compare `CSetVariableCommand::Execute` (0x1532C0), the same shape over the same field layout, which writes the live object directly.

The command does get posted and does get executed: the loopback post's gate is command slot 14, which for this class is the three-instruction `return this->country.id (+0x40) != 0` at 0x1530C0 - shared with CSetVariableCommand and CSetCountryControllerCommand, so described here rather than named - and any real country has a non-zero id.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x152C30-0x152E06 instruction by instruction; retsBefore empty; vtable.py --holding gives one holder, slot 6. The two allocated classes are identified by the vftables their constructors write, 0x15C9880 and 0x15C98A4, resolved through the RTTI export to CAddCountryFlagChange and CRemoveCountryFlagChange. CCountry+0xCCC is already recorded as `history`. What would show it wrong: a write to CCountry+0x180 anywhere in the body, or a call from AddEntry (0x1F4660) into the entry's slot 7 - neither exists; AddEntry's own recorded entry says it allocates a node and returns.

addresses.name: CSetFlagCommand::GetTypeId
addresses.comment: Slot 7, one holder, the whole of `mov eax, 0x37D; ret`. **0x37D is the save token `set_country_flag`** - the same token `CAddCountryFlagChange::SaveContents` (0x1EF2C0) writes - so a command's type id is drawn from the save-token space. This is the value the post writes to the wire ahead of the serialised command and the value `CCommand::type_id` (+0x2C) holds. CSetVariableCommand's equivalent is at 0x153320 and returns 0x40F, `set_variable`.
addresses.evidence: Six bytes read at 0x152E10; vtable.py --holding gives one holder, slot 7. Token 0x37D resolved through ghidra/saveTokens.json. What would show it wrong: a second holder of the body, or 0x37D resolving to something other than set_country_flag.

addresses.name: CSetFlagCommand::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2, one holder. 0x152E20 to the `ret 4` at 0x152F23, twelve int3, then LoadKey at 0x152F30. **It writes three keys**, which is what fixes the class's layout: `country` (token 0x24D) from the four-character tag at `this+0x3C`, `flagType` (token 0x1BF) from the Hoi3CString at `this+0x44`, and `value` (token 0x2A6) from the byte at `this+0x60`, written as the literals `yes` ([0x15C1914]) and `no` ([0x15C1918]). The base `CCommand::SaveContents` (0x67BB80) runs first, at 0x152E47.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x152E20-0x152F23; the three `mov ecx, <token>; call 0x67A1B0` pairs read directly, tokens resolved through ghidra/saveTokens.json. It agrees key for key with LoadKey's three cases at 0x152F30, which is an independent reading of the same layout.

addresses.name: CSetFlagCommand::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSetFlagCommand::LoadKey(CSetFlagCommand* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**Three keys, not two** - corrected 2026-10-06 by reading the switch off the bytes; `definitions.py` had reported `country` and `flagType` and missed the third. The binary search at 0x152F53 subtracts 0x1BF, then 0x8E, then 0x59, so the cases are tokens **0x1BF `flagType`**, **0x24D `country`** and **0x2A6 `value`**, and each one names its own field:

- `flagType` (0x153007): `Hoi3CString::assign(this + 0x44, parse->value.text (+0x22C), strlen)` at 0x153024
- `country` (0x152FA1): `CCountryDataBase::GetTag` (0x118480) at 0x152FE6, its result copied as two dwords into `this+0x3C` and `this+0x40`
- `value` (0x152F87): `ParseBool` (0x67B410) on `this+0x60`

Anything else goes to `CCommand::LoadKey` (0x67BC80). Four exits, all `ret 8`: 0x152F84, 0x152F9E, 0x153004 and 0x153038. The same three cases, with the same tokens and the same offsets, are `CSetVariableCommand::LoadKey` (0x153460) - including the key spelled `flagType` for what is a variable name there.
addresses.revises: the key list said two keys; the switch has three cases and each is read here with the field it writes
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x152F30-0x153038; the three `sub eax, N` / `je` pairs give the tokens, resolved through ghidra/saveTokens.json. Cross-checked against SaveContents (0x152E20), which writes exactly those three tokens from exactly those three offsets.

addresses.name: CSetVariableCommand::Execute
addresses.comment:
**Slot 6, one holder (vftable 0x15C3E64), and the working control for `CSetFlagCommand::Execute` (0x152C30)** - the same constructor shape and the same field layout, writing the live object instead of the history. 0x1532C0 to two bare `ret`s at 0x15330C and 0x15331E, one int3, then slot 7 at 0x153320; both exits restore the same frame, so they are two exits of one function.

It resolves the country as `CCountryDataBase ([0x1A855A4]) ->+0x16C[this->country.id (+0x40)]`, takes the `CVariables` held **by value at `CCountry +0x1AC`** - the object the registered accessor `CCountry::GetVariables` (0xCCD40, `lea eax,[ecx+0x1AC]; ret`) returns - and calls **slot 1** of it with `&this->name (+0x44)`. On a hit it writes `this->value (+0x60)` straight into the found variable's payload at `+0x1C` (0x153303); on a miss it calls `CVariables::AddVariable` (0x76FB0), which is the call site that entry already lists as "CSetVariableCommand slot 6 (0x1532C0) at 0x153313".

So the two commands differ in exactly one respect, and it is not their shape: this one reaches `CCountry +0x1AC` and the flag one reaches `CCountry +0xCCC`.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1532C0-0x15331E end to end; vtable.py --holding gives one holder, slot 6. 0xCCD40 is `lea eax,[ecx+0x1AC]; ret` and is the luabind registration CCountry::GetVariables, which ties +0x1AC to CVariables independently of this reading. The AddVariable call at 0x153313 is already recorded from the other side.

addresses.name: CSetVariableCommand::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSetVariableCommand::LoadKey(CSetVariableCommand* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**Three keys, not one** - corrected 2026-10-06 off the bytes; `definitions.py` had reported only `country`. The switch is byte for byte the shape of `CSetFlagCommand::LoadKey` (0x152F30): `sub eax, 0x1BF`, `sub eax, 0x8E`, `sub eax, 0x59`, so tokens **0x1BF**, **0x24D `country`** and **0x2A6 `value`**.

The interesting one is the first: the key is spelled **`flagType`** here too, and its handler at 0x15353A assigns into `this+0x44`, which on this class is the *variable name*. The engine reuses the flag command's key for it. `value` (0x1534B9) goes through `ParseFixedPoint` (0x67B540) into `this+0x60`, so it is thousandths; `country` (0x1534D3) uses `CCountryDataBase::GetTag` (0x118480) into `this+0x3C`/`+0x40`. Anything else to `CCommand::LoadKey` (0x67BC80). Four exits, all `ret 8`: 0x1534B6, 0x1534D0, 0x153537 and 0x15356A.
addresses.revises: the key list said one key, `country`; the switch has three cases, and the first is the flag command's `flagType` token reused for the variable name
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x153460-0x15356A; the three `sub eax, N` / `je` pairs give the tokens, resolved through ghidra/saveTokens.json. The handler offsets match CSetFlagCommand's case for case, which is the cross-check. What would show it wrong: token 0x1BF resolving to something other than flagType, or the 0x15353A handler writing an offset other than +0x44.

addresses.name: CAddCountryFlagChange::CAddCountryFlagChange
addresses.comment: 0x1EF220 to the `ret 4` at 0x1EF24D. `this` in ECX, the country on the stack, `this` back in EAX. Calls the base `CCountryHistoryEntry::CCountryHistoryEntry` (0x1EEA40) with the country, writes its own vftable 0x15C9880, then constructs the Hoi3CString at `this+0x10` through 0x65A700 (0x1EF23F). **Two callers**: `CSetFlagCommand::Execute` at 0x152C87, and 0x1ED218 inside the country history's own entry factory (`CCountryHistory` slot 9, 0x1ECA90) - so the class exists both to be loaded out of a history block and to be filed by the command. In no virtual table; recorded under the class because it writes that class's table.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1EF220-0x1EF24D. The vftable 0x15C9880 resolves through the RTTI export to CAddCountryFlagChange and to nothing else. findRefs --callers gives exactly the two call sites.

addresses.name: CAddCountryFlagChange::Apply
addresses.comment:
**Slot 7, one holder, and this is where a country flag actually gets set** - the write `CSetFlagCommand::Execute` does not do. 0x1EF250 to the one `ret 4` at 0x1EF2BC, no interior `ret`. The bool is the direction `CHistoryContainer::ApplyRange` (0x1F47C0) and `ApplyAll` (0x1F4830) pass: 1 to apply, 0 to undo.

Both arms resolve the country the same way - `CCountry::GetFlags` (0xCCD30, `lea eax,[ecx+0x180]; ret`) on the `CCountry*` at `this+0xC` (0x1EF273) - and take the flag name from the Hoi3CString at `this+0x10` through its `c_str` (0xC3B0, at 0x1EF265). Forward calls `CFlags_SetFlag` (0x4D6A0) at 0x1EF288, which creates the flag if it is not in the tree; backward calls `CFlags_ClearFlag` (0x4D6C0) at 0x1EF2B3, which does not. `CRemoveCountryFlagChange::Apply` (0x1EF380) is the same body with the two arms swapped.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1EF250-0x1EF2BC; vtable.py --holding gives one holder, slot 7, in the CAddCountryFlagChange table. 0xCCD30 is the luabind-registered CCountry::GetFlags, which is independent of this reading. The bool's meaning comes from the already-recorded ApplyRange and ApplyAll, which pass 1 forwards and 0 backwards.

addresses.name: CAddCountryFlagChange::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2, one holder. 0x1EF2C0 to the `ret 4` at 0x1EF2E0: it writes the one key **`set_country_flag` (token 0x37D)** with the Hoi3CString at `this+0x10` as its value, through the string writer 0x679210. That is what a flag set this way leaves behind - a line in the country's `history` block in the savegame - and it is also why 0x37D doubles as `CSetFlagCommand`'s type id (0x152E10). `CRemoveCountryFlagChange::SaveContents` (0x1EF3F0) is the same with token **0x37E, `clr_country_flag`**.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1EF2C0-0x1EF2E0 and 0x1EF3F0-0x1EF410; the `mov ecx, 0x37D` / `mov ecx, 0x37E` immediates read directly and resolved through ghidra/saveTokens.json.

addresses.name: CRemoveCountryFlagChange::CRemoveCountryFlagChange
addresses.comment: The mirror of 0x1EF220, instruction for instruction, differing only in the vftable it writes (0x15C98A4). 0x1EF2F0 to the `ret 4` at 0x1EF31D; the string at `this+0x10` is constructed at 0x1EF30F. Two callers: `CSetFlagCommand::Execute` at 0x152D28 and 0x1ED2C6 in the history entry factory. In no virtual table.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1EF2F0-0x1EF31D; the vftable resolves through the RTTI export to CRemoveCountryFlagChange alone; findRefs --callers gives the two sites.

addresses.name: CountryFlagChange_SetName
addresses.comment: Eleven instructions, 0x1EF360 to the `ret 4` at 0x1EF37A: `change->+0x10 = *name`, through the string assignment at 0x1060 (`std::string::operator=`, which takes its source in EAX). **Called twice, both from `CSetFlagCommand::Execute`** (0x152C98 and 0x152D39), once on each of the two change classes, which is why it carries no class name - the two holders share the body and the string sits at +0x10 on both. In no virtual table.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1EF360-0x1EF37A; findRefs --callers gives exactly the two sites, which construct objects of two different classes; vtable.py --holding reports no table. 0x1060 is already recorded as std::string::operator= with the source in EAX.

addresses.name: CRemoveCountryFlagChange::Apply
addresses.comment: Slot 7, one holder. The mirror of `CAddCountryFlagChange::Apply` (0x1EF250): forward (bool 1) calls `CFlags_ClearFlag` (0x4D6C0) at 0x1EF3B6 and the undo arm calls `CFlags_SetFlag` (0x4D6A0) at 0x1EF3E3. The country comes from `this+0xC` (0x1EF3A3) and the name from the string at `this+0x10` (0x1EF395). 0x1EF380 to the one `ret 4` at 0x1EF3EC.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1EF380-0x1EF3EC; the two calls read at 0x1EF3B6 and 0x1EF3E3, swapped relative to 0x1EF250; vtable.py --holding gives one holder, slot 7.

addresses.name: CRemoveCountryFlagChange::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2, one holder. The mirror of 0x1EF2C0, writing the key **`clr_country_flag` (token 0x37E)** with the Hoi3CString at `this+0x10`. 0x1EF3F0 to the `ret 4` at 0x1EF410.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1EF3F0-0x1EF410; the `mov ecx, 0x37E` read directly at 0x1EF3FF and resolved through ghidra/saveTokens.json.

addresses.name: CCountryHistoryEntry::CCountryHistoryEntry
addresses.comment: The base of all twenty-odd `C*Change` classes that hang off a country's history. 0x1EEA40 to the `ret 4` at 0x1EEA67, `this` in ECX and the country on the stack. Calls `CHistoryEntry::CHistoryEntry` (0x1F4550), writes its own vftable 0x15C96EC, and stores the country at **`this+0xC`** (0x1EEA5E) - the field every derived Apply reads to find the object it changes. In no virtual table.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1EEA40-0x1EEA67. The vftable resolves through the RTTI export to CCountryHistoryEntry. +0xC is read as the country by both flag-change Applies (0x1EF273 and 0x1EF3A3), which is the independent check.

addresses.name: CHistoryEntry::CHistoryEntry
addresses.comment: Seven instructions, 0x1F4550 to the bare `ret` at 0x1F4573, receiver in **EAX** and nothing on the stack. Bumps the live-entry counter at [0x1A855F0], writes `CPersistent::token (+4) = 0x18D` - the same `none` id the whole CDiplomaticAction family carries - its own vftable 0x15C9E8C, and then `this+8` **twice**: once with the literal 0x29C55C0 and immediately again from [0x170C2B8], the engine's null-date global that CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor also uses. The first store is dead. So `+8` is the entry's date and it starts at the epoch. In no virtual table.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1F4550-0x1F4573. +8 is read as the date by the already-recorded CHistoryContainer::AddEntry (0x1F4660, "the current tail entry's date (entry+8)") and ApplyRange (0x1F47C0), and written as the current tick by CSetFlagCommand::Execute at 0x152DEA, as CCountry::ChangeNeutrality and CFaction::AddCountry already do with their own entries - four independent witnesses to the same offset. [0x170C2B8] is already recorded as the engine's null date.

addresses.name: CFlags_SetFlag
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CFlags_SetFlag(CFlags* flags@ESI, const char* name@EAX)
addresses.comment:
**Set a flag, creating it if it is not there** - the find-or-create wrapper around `CFlags_AddFlag` (0x4D640), whose own entry already mentions it as "0x4D6A0 nearby". 0x4D6A0 to two bare `ret`s at 0x4D6B6 and 0x4D6BE, both in the same frame; both arguments are in registers, the container in ESI and the name in EAX (moved straight to EDI, which is the register `CFlags_AddFlag` wants it in). It calls container slot 2 - the recorded `GuiTypeTree_Find` (0x67DEE0) - with the name, writes `CFlag::is_set (+0x1C) = 1` on a hit, and tail-calls `CFlags_AddFlag` on a miss.

**Four callers, all of them history-change Applies**: 0x1EF288 (`CAddCountryFlagChange::Apply`), 0x1EF3E3 (`CRemoveCountryFlagChange::Apply`, its undo arm), 0x1EF528 and 0x1EF7DA (the global- and province-flag changes). So this wrapper is the history subsystem's door into `CFlags`, where the three `set_*_flag` event effects go to `CFlags_AddFlag` directly. Recorded class-free: it is in no virtual table and the container is only ever reached as a `CFlags`-shaped object, exactly as 0x4D640 is.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4D6A0-0x4D6BE; findRefs --callers gives the four sites and vtable.py --holding reports no table. The slot-2 call and the +0x1C write are the same two steps CSetCountryFlagEffect::Execute (0x5A4970) already records.

addresses.name: CFlags_ClearFlag
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CFlags_ClearFlag(CFlags* flags@ECX, const char* name@EDX)
addresses.comment: Eight instructions, 0x4D6C0 to the bare `ret` at 0x4D6D0, container in ECX and name in EDX. Container slot 2 (`GuiTypeTree_Find`, 0x67DEE0) with the name, and `CFlag::is_set (+0x1C) = 0` on a hit; **on a miss it does nothing and creates nothing**, which is the same asymmetry `CClrCountryFlagEffect::Execute` (0x5A49E0) already records on the effect side. Four callers, all history-change Applies: 0x1EF2B3, 0x1EF3B6, 0x1EF5DA, 0x1EF726. Class-free for the same reason as 0x4D6A0.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4D6C0-0x4D6D0; findRefs --callers gives the four sites; vtable.py --holding reports no table.

addresses.name: CRef_Resolve
addresses.comment:
**What a `CRef<T>` dereference compiles to, and it can return NULL.** Receiver in EAX, bare `ret`, result in EAX; 0x19A190 to 0x19A1D6, two exits. It copies the ref's `+4` (the persistent type) and `+8` (the persistent id) into a two-dword stack key, picks the registry by `type > 0x1268` - [0x1A857F0] above, [0x1A857F4] at or below, the same split the recorded `FindPersistentById` (0x69DA00) describes - calls that lookup, and returns `result - 8`, or **0** when the table is null or the lookup misses.

**170 direct callers**, so this is one body shared by every `CRef<T>` instantiation; recorded class-free. `CRef_ResolveAndCache` (0x2DE10) is the same computation with the receiver in ESI and the result also written back to `ref->+0`, and is what a validity test compiles to - 155 callers. Note that **neither is a guard**: the caller has to test the result, and `CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::Apply` (0x6395B0) is a place where one call is tested and an earlier one is not.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x19A190-0x19A1D6 and 0x2DE10-0x2DE59; the registry split and the NULL-on-miss return are already established in FindPersistentById's own entry (0x69DA00, "the result comes back in EAX and is NULL when nothing matches"). findRefs --callers gives 170 and 155. vtable.py --holding reports no table for either, and neither address appears in ghidra/luabind.json, so trap 4 is clear in both of its forms.

addresses.name: CRef_ResolveAndCache
addresses.comment: `CRef_Resolve` (0x19A190) with the receiver in **ESI** and one extra store: the resolved pointer, or 0, is written back to `ref->cached (+0)` before being returned. Bare `ret`, result in EAX, 0x2DE10 to 0x2DE59, two exits. 155 direct callers, so class-free. This is the form a validity test uses - `CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::IsValid` (0x63AD90) calls it and returns false on 0.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x2DE10-0x2DE59; the only difference from 0x19A190 is the receiver register and the `mov [esi], eax` on both exits. findRefs --callers gives 155; no virtual table and no luabind registration.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::PostAction
addresses.comment:
**The one route from a script to a diplomatic action, and it has no gate of its own.** Already named by the Lua half (`void PostAction(CEU3AI&, CDiplomaticAction&)`) and already mentioned in `CAIForeignMinister::DoWork`'s comment as "handing it to 0x89A750 with the OwnerAI"; this adds the body. 0x49A750 to the `ret 4` at 0x49A788, `this` in ECX and the action on the stack.

Four steps, every one of them a virtual call:

    ecx = this + 0x20; call 0x2610      ; a shared accessor thunk -> the CCountry
    esi = country->+0xF1C               ; the network/session manager
    edi = action->slot 6                ; CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand (0x60E890)
    eax = manager->slot 18              ; the session
    (session->+0x38)->slot 6 (edi)      ; the channel's Post

So it is **exactly** what the hourly AI pass at 0x682BC2 does with the result of `MakeCommand` - the same two slots in the same order - and it does **not** go through `CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction` (0xE61C0). The command is posted straight onto the session channel, drained by the pump, and `CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute` (0x60E120) runs it; that function's slot 13 `IsValid` test is therefore the only thing between a script and the action's own slot 7. `country+0xF1C` and `session+0x38` are the pair `CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand`'s entry already names.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x49A750-0x49A788. The two slot numbers are read off the displacements: [vft+0x18] is slot 6 and [vft+0x48] is slot 18. That slot 6 on a CDiplomaticAction is MakeCommand and that country+0xF1C's slot 18 gives the session with its channel at +0x38 are both already recorded, in MakeCommand's own entry, which describes the hourly AI pass taking the same two steps - so this is a second, independent sighting of that sequence rather than a fresh claim. vtable.py --holding reports no table, consistent with its being a free method. What would show it wrong: a gate between the post and Execute other than the pump's turn-stamp and double-command checks, which were not re-read here.

addresses.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::CSendExpeditionaryForceAction
addresses.signature: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction* __stdcall CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::CSendExpeditionaryForceAction(CSendExpeditionaryForceAction* this, CCountryTag actor, CCountryTag recipient)
addresses.comment:
**The two-tag constructor the Lua API registers, and the reason the registration cannot work.** 0x639260 to the `ret 0x14` at 0x6393A4; `this` and the two by-value 8-byte `CCountryTag`s all arrive on the stack, and `this` comes back in EAX. It fills the `CDiplomaticAction` base the way the family's other factories do - actor at +8/+0xC, recipient at +0x10/+0x14, `type` (+0x18) = 0 PROPOSE, `date` and `last_command_date` (+0x1C/+0x20) from `g_CCurrentGameState->tick (+0xBDC)`, `value` (+0x24) = 1, `persistent_id` (+4) = 0x18D - writes its own vftable 0x15FB934, and then the two fields that matter here:

    [this+0x28] = 1                 ClaimType = SEND          (0x63933C)
    [this+0x2C] = 0                 the CRef's cached pointer  (0x639355)
    [this+0x30] = [0x1A8CC94]       the CRef's persistent type (0x63935D)
    [this+0x34] = [0x1A8CC98]       the CRef's persistent id   (0x639366)
    [this+0x38] = ""                the CRef's name

Those two globals are the shared null-`CRef` statics: 175 and 161 occurrences in `.text` and **not one of them a write**, and they sit past `.data`'s raw bytes, so they are permanently zero. So the constructed action's `unit` is a null ref, and nothing a script can call will change it - `GetUnit`, `GetClaimType` and `GetTag` are the class's only three registrations and all three are getters.

Two neighbours share the layout and are not recorded separately: 0x639400 is a longer constructor that writes the same vftable and the same `ClaimType = 1` and null ref, and 0x6394E0 is the copy constructor, which copies +8 through +0x34 and the string at +0x38 - it is what slot 16's clone uses.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x639260-0x6393A4; the vftable 0x15FB934 resolves through the RTTI export to this class alone, and image.findValue(0x15FB934) over .text gives exactly three writers, the three constructors named here. The claim that the two globals are never written was checked by decoding every one of their 175 and 161 .text occurrences and testing whether the global is the destination operand, with a positive control: the same scan over 0x1A89790 finds 1,928 writes. What would show it wrong: a write to either global from outside .text, or a .data initialiser - the addresses lie beyond the last byte of .data's raw data, so there is none in the file.

addresses.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::IsValid
addresses.comment:
**Slot 13, one holder, and the instruction that decides whether this class can be used from script.** 0x63AD90 to two bare `ret`s at 0x63ADF0 (false) and 0x63AE41, result in AL.

    0x63ADF1  lea esi, [edi + 0x2C]      ; &this->unit
    0x63ADF4  call 0x2DE10               ; CRef_ResolveAndCache
    0x63ADF9  test eax, eax
    0x63ADFB  je   0x63ADE9              ; -> xor al, al; ret

So **an action whose `unit` ref does not resolve is invalid**, and `CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute` (0x60E120) tests slot 13 first and does nothing at all when it is false. A Lua-constructed action therefore cannot do anything: the constructor (0x639260) leaves the ref null, nothing registered can fill it, and slot 7 `Apply` is never reached.

The rest: when `value` (+0x24) is set it first requires the two countries' factions (`CCountry +0xD8`) to differ and, if they do, `actor->+0xE28[recipient_id]->+0x14` to be non-zero, failing to false; and when the ref does resolve it answers `unit->+0x1F4 != 0`. The second resolve is open-coded rather than another call, with the same `type > 0x1268` registry split.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x63AD90-0x63AE41 instruction by instruction; vtable.py --holding gives one holder, slot 13, in the 0x15FB934 table. That slot 13 is the gate is not inferred from the name: CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute's recorded entry already says "a->IsValid() (slot 13) at 0xA0E135 - false and nothing at all happens". What would show it wrong: a caller of slot 7 that does not go through that command, which was not searched exhaustively - slot 7's displacement has 1,043 call sites image-wide, so a targeted search is the honest next step.

addresses.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::GetTag
addresses.comment:
**Slot 20, and the only place `ClaimType` changes anything a player sees.** 0x63B040 to the one `ret 4` at 0x63B26B; `this` in ECX, the return buffer on the stack, and that buffer comes back in EAX. The luabind registration `CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::GetTag` reaches it through the recorded slot-20 thunk at 0x598400.

It picks one of three localisation keys and runs it through the text formatter (0x682490 / 0x682E40 / 0x687020):

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `value` (+0x24) non-zero (test at 0x63B063) | **`SENDEXPED`** - whatever ClaimType says |
| `value` zero, `ClaimType` (+0x28) == 0 TAKE (test at 0x63B113) | **`RETRIEVEEXPED`** |
| `value` zero, `ClaimType` != 0 SEND | **`RESENDEXPED`** |

So the offer itself always reads as `SENDEXPED`, and TAKE/SEND only distinguish the two kinds of *withdrawal*. That is consistent with the field's only other reader, slot 11's tooltip at 0x63ACE4, which picks `RETRIEVEEXPEDDESC` the same way.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x63B040-0x63B26B; the three string literals read at 0x63B06E, 0x63B12E and 0x63B1C5 and the two branches at 0x63B063 (`cmp byte [ecx+0x24], 0`) and 0x63B113 (`cmp dword [ecx+0x28], 0`). A grep of every instruction in 0x63A860-0x63B3D8 for a `[reg + 0x28]` operand gives exactly two reads, this one and the tooltip's, plus SaveContents' read at 0x63B2B8 and LoadKey's store at 0x63B362.

addresses.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::GetUnit
addresses.comment:
**The registered getter, and what it copies is what fixes the field's size.** 0x63B380 to the `ret 4` at 0x63B3C1; `this` in ECX, the return buffer on the stack, the buffer back in EAX. It copies `this+0x2C`, `this+0x30` and `this+0x34` into `out+0`, `out+4` and `out+8`, then constructs `out+0xC` from the Hoi3CString at `this+0x38`. So the `CRef<CUnit>` is **one by-value member spanning +0x2C to +0x53** - three dwords and a 0x1C-byte string - and not a bare pointer at +0x2C. luabind's registered return type `CRef<CUnit>` agrees.

There is no setter. This, `GetClaimType` (the folded body at 0x63B3D0) and `GetTag` are the class's only three registrations, so the member is readable from script and not writable, and the two-tag constructor (0x639260) leaves it null.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x63B380-0x63B3C1. The four destinations in `out` and the four sources in `this` are read directly, and the constructor at 0x639260 writes the same four slots in the same order. The absence of a setter is from ghidra/luabind.json: the class carries three `method` registrations and one constructor, and a search of the file for the class name finds nothing else.

addresses.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::LoadKey(CSendExpeditionaryForceAction* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**Two keys, and now with the field each one lands in** - which is the point, because they are the only two writers of the fields the Lua constructor leaves empty. Three exits, all `ret 8`: 0x63B327, 0x63B36A and 0x63B37C.

- **`unit`** (token 0x256, case at 0x63B317): `lea esi, [edi + 0x2C]` at 0x63B31A and `0x1EC150` with the parse context - so the key fills the `CRef<CUnit>` in place
- **`action`** (token 0x2ED, case at 0x63B331): `sscanf(parse->value.text (+0x22C), "%i", &out)` and `[this+0x28] = out` at 0x63B362, so `ClaimType` is a plain integer in the file, 0 TAKE or 1 SEND
- anything else to `CDiplomaticAction::LoadKey` (0x60E690)

So the only ways `unit` is ever non-null are a save or history block carrying the key, the copy constructor at 0x6394E0, and whatever the AI does before `CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand` - never a script.
addresses.revises: the key list was right; this adds the field each case writes, which is what settles that nothing but the loader fills +0x2C
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x63B300-0x63B37C; the two `cmp eax, <token>` immediates read directly and resolved through ghidra/saveTokens.json; the destination offsets are the `lea esi,[edi+0x2C]` at 0x63B31A and the `mov [edi+0x28], edx` at 0x63B362. Cross-checked against SaveContents (slot 2, 0x63B270), which reads +0x28 at 0x63B2B8 and +0x30/+0x34 at 0x63B294/0x63B297.

addresses.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
**Slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB934), read end to end 2026-10-06 - 1,226 instructions, 0x6395B0 to the one bare `ret` at 0x63A853, `retsBefore` empty, 12 int3, then slot 11 at 0x63A860.** `this` in ECX and then in frame slot [esp+0x20], nothing on the stack. The earlier `inferred` reading was right about the name and about every call it listed; what follows corrects nothing and adds the order.

**It is in three parts.** (1) A message is built - `ACTOR`, `RECIPIENT`, `RECPIENT` (the engine's own typo), `MESSAGE_HEAD_CHAN`, `MESSENGER` and `UNIT` substitutions, the last of them at 0x639DD1 taking `&this->unit (+0x2C)` through `CRef_Resolve` (0x19A190) and then calling **slot 7 of the resolved `CUnit` with no null test at all** (`mov edx,[eax]` at 0x639DE8). (2) At 0x639EBB the unit ref is resolved again through `CRef_ResolveAndCache` (0x2DE10) and **this** result is tested: zero jumps to the epilogue at 0x63A83F and the action does nothing. So the guard is 0xEA bytes *after* the dereference - harmless in practice only because slot 13 `IsValid` (0x63AD90) refuses a null-unit action before `CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute` (0x60E120) ever reaches slot 7. (3) The work, keyed on the base's `type` (+0x18) and `value` (+0x24), not on `ClaimType`:

- `type == 0` PROPOSE and `value` set (0x639ED5): the influence cost, `-GetDefines()->diplomacy (+0xBC)->+0xAC` (EXPEDITION_INFLUENCE_COST), through 0xF4E50 on the actor
- `type == 2` ACCEPT and `value` set (0x639F2F): the hand-over. `0x1B9A30(unit, 1)`, then `unit->+0x294` from the defines, then - only when `unit->+0x290` is still zero - `unit->+0x28C`/`+0x290` saved from the other country's `+0x124`/`+0x128`, which is how the brigade finds its way home; then 0xE0860, 0xE0830 and 0xE06F0 move it between the two countries' unit lists, and 0x1D3840 runs when `unit->+0x1EC` is set
- `type == 2` ACCEPT and `value` clear (0x63A519): the return leg, keyed `OUREXPDEC` and `EXPOTHER`

**`ClaimType` (+0x28) is never read in the whole body** - a grep of all 1,226 instructions for a `[reg + 0x28]` operand on any base but ESP returns nothing, while the same grep finds `[reg + 0x18]` and `[reg + 0x24]` at fourteen sites. So the direction of an expedition is carried by `value`, and TAKE/SEND only choose a localisation key in slot 20. EXPEDITION_RETURN_TIME (+0xB0) is read and EXPEDITION_RECLAIM_TIME (+0xB4) is not, as the earlier entry said; the news keys are `OUREXPACC`, `OUREXPDEC` and `EXPOTHER`, with `diplomaticsuccess`/`diplomaticfailure` as the sound.
addresses.revises: was `inferred`, with its own comment saying the body had not been read instruction by instruction; it now has been, and the entry gains the order of operations, the unguarded dereference at 0x639DE8, the guard at 0x639ECB, and the negative that ClaimType is not read here
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x6395B0-0x63A853 in full (1,226 instructions) and walked the block graph with cfg.py: the block at 0x639DAF that holds the UNIT substitution is entered only by fall-through from 0x639DA0, and every branch between the entry and it is a two-way SSO diamond that reconverges, so the dereference is unconditional. retsBefore(0x6395B0, 0x63A853) is empty. The ClaimType negative carries its control: the same regular expression over the same dump finds `[esi + 0x18]`, `[esi + 0x24]`, `[ecx + 0x18]` and `[eax + 0x24]` at fourteen sites, so it can see a field read on this object; `0x28` appears only as `[esp + 0x28]`. What would show it wrong: a read of +0x28 through a base the dump spells differently, or a path to slot 7 that bypasses the command's IsValid gate.

structs.name: CSetFlagCommand
structs.comment: The Lua-registered `CSetFlagCommand(CCountryTag, const CString&, bool)`. Its three own fields are the three constructor arguments, and its Execute (0x152C30) files them as a country-history change rather than setting a flag.
structs.evidence: RTTI gives CCommand as the base at offset 0 and 0x15C3E24 as the class's only table, 15 slots. The three offsets are each written by LoadKey (0x152F30) and read by SaveContents (0x152E20) and Execute (0x152C30).

structs.name: CSetVariableCommand
structs.comment: The Lua-registered `CSetVariableCommand(CCountryTag, const CString&, CFixedPoint)`, and the working control for CSetFlagCommand: the same three fields at the same three offsets, and an Execute (0x1532C0) that writes the live CVariables at CCountry +0x1AC.
structs.evidence: RTTI gives CCommand at offset 0 and 0x15C3E64 as the only table, 15 slots. The offsets are written by LoadKey (0x153460) and read by Execute (0x1532C0); they are the same three as CSetFlagCommand's, which is the point of the comparison.

structs.name: CHistoryEntry
structs.comment: One dated change in a CHistoryContainer. Slot 6 is the save token and slot 7 is Apply(bool forward); both are _purecall on this base, so every leaf supplies them.
structs.evidence: RTTI gives CPersistent at offset 0 and 0x15C9E8C as the only table, 8 slots, which is the one CHistoryEntry::CHistoryEntry (0x1F4550) writes. Slots 6 and 7 in it both hold _purecall (0xB961D5).

structs.name: CCountryHistoryEntry
structs.comment: The base of the twenty-odd `C*Change` classes in a country's history - CAddCountryFlagChange, CGovernmentChange, CLawChange, CDissentChange and the rest. It adds the CCountry* the change applies to.
structs.evidence: RTTI gives CHistoryEntry at offset 0 and 0x15C96EC as the only table, which is the one the constructor at 0x1EEA40 writes.

structs.name: CAddCountryFlagChange
structs.comment: `set_country_flag` as a history entry: the thing CSetFlagCommand::Execute (0x152C30) builds when its bool is set, and one of only four objects in the image whose Apply sets a country flag through CFlags_SetFlag.
structs.evidence: RTTI gives CCountryHistoryEntry at offset 0 and 0x15C9880 as the only table. The size is measured, not guessed: both call sites of the constructor allocate with `push 0x2C; call operator new`, and +0x10 plus the 0x1C-byte Hoi3CString there is exactly 0x2C.

structs.name: CRemoveCountryFlagChange
structs.comment: `clr_country_flag` as a history entry, the mirror of CAddCountryFlagChange and the other half of what CSetFlagCommand::Execute can build.
structs.evidence: RTTI gives CCountryHistoryEntry at offset 0 and 0x15C98A4 as the only table. The size is measured the same way: `push 0x2C` at both construction sites, and +0x10 plus a 0x1C-byte string is 0x2C.

structs.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction
structs.comment: Lending or reclaiming a brigade. Lua registers a `(CCountryTag, CCountryTag)` constructor and three getters, and no setter for the unit, so a script-built one is always invalid - see IsValid (0x63AD90). ClaimType at +0x28 is already named here by the Lua half; this declaration adds the base, the table and the `unit` member beside it.
structs.evidence: RTTI gives CDiplomaticAction at offset 0 and 0x15FB934 as the only table, 22 slots. Every one of the class's own bodies lies in 0x639260-0x63B3D3 and the table's entries all point into that range.

structs.name: CRef
structs.comment: The by-value shape of a `CRef<T>` - the engine's weak handle to a persistent object: a cached pointer, the two halves of the save file's `id = { type = N id = N }` pair, and a name. It is **not** a pointer: a field of this type occupies 0x28 bytes, which is why CSendExpeditionaryForceAction's unit spans +0x2C to +0x53. Resolving one is CRef_Resolve (0x19A190) or CRef_ResolveAndCache (0x2DE10), and both return NULL on a miss, so a `CRef` member is never safe to dereference without a test.
structs.evidence: Read off two sides of the same object. CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::GetUnit (0x63B380) copies this+0x2C/+0x30/+0x34 into out+0/+4/+8 and constructs out+0xC from the string at this+0x38, and the constructor at 0x639260 writes the same four slots in the same order; the two resolvers read +4 and +8 as the type/id key that the recorded FindPersistentById (0x69DA00) takes, and 0x2DE10 writes its result back to +0. `size` is deliberately left undeclared: only this one instantiation was measured.

struct_fields.name: country
struct_fields.comment: The country whose flag is meant, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the four-character tag at +0x3C and the id at +0x40. Loaded from the save key `country` (token 0x24D) through CCountryDataBase::GetTag at 0x152FE6; written by the Lua constructor's first argument. Execute indexes `g_CCountryDataBase->+0x16C` with the id, and command slot 14 (0x1530C0) answers `id != 0`, which is what lets the post accept the command.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's `country` case copies GetTag's two dwords to +0x3C and +0x40 (0x152FED, 0x152FF3); SaveContents reads the tag at +0x3C as a C string (0x152E4C) and Execute reads both halves (0x152C6B).

struct_fields.name: flagType
struct_fields.comment: The flag name, under the save key's own spelling (token 0x1BF, `flagType`). A 0x1C-byte Hoi3CString, so it runs to +0x5F with the bool on the next byte. **It is a free string and not a lookup into any database**: LoadKey assigns it from the raw value text and Execute hands it straight to the change object's own string, which CAddCountryFlagChange::Apply (0x1EF250) then passes to the flag tree. Nothing resolves it against `CFlagType`, whose LoadKey (0x4450B0) takes the single key `size` and is about flag images.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's case at 0x153024 is `Hoi3CString::assign(this+0x44, parse->+0x22C, strlen)`; SaveContents writes it at 0x152EB8; Execute passes `&this[0x44]` to CountryFlagChange_SetName at 0x152C92. The negative - no database lookup - comes from reading the whole of Execute, 0x152C30 to 0x152E06, which contains no database call and no reference to [0x1A855A4] other than the country lookup.

struct_fields.name: value
struct_fields.comment: Set or clear, the Lua constructor's third argument. The one branch in Execute (`cmp byte ptr [esi+0x60], 0` at 0x152C52): set builds a CAddCountryFlagChange, clear builds a CRemoveCountryFlagChange. Saved as `value = yes` / `value = no` (token 0x2A6) and loaded through ParseBool (0x67B410).
struct_fields.evidence: Read at 0x152C52 in Execute and at 0x152EC1 in SaveContents, written by LoadKey's `value` case at 0x152F87. Its width is a byte in all three.

struct_fields.name: country
struct_fields.comment: The country whose variable is meant; tag at +0x3C, id at +0x40, loaded from `country` (token 0x24D) through CCountryDataBase::GetTag at 0x153518. The same offset and the same shape as CSetFlagCommand's.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey copies GetTag's two dwords to +0x3C and +0x40 (0x15351F, 0x153526); Execute reads +0x40 as the index into the country database at 0x1532D5.

struct_fields.name: name
struct_fields.comment: The variable's name, 0x1C bytes. Loaded from the key **`flagType`** (token 0x1BF) - the flag command's key reused - at 0x153556, and handed to slot 1 of the country's CVariables by Execute at 0x1532FA.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's first case assigns into this+0x44 at 0x153553/0x153556; Execute takes `lea esi,[ecx+0x44]` at 0x1532D8 and passes it to the find.

struct_fields.name: value
struct_fields.comment: The value to store, in thousandths - loaded through ParseFixedPoint (0x67B540) from the key `value` (token 0x2A6) at 0x1534BC. Execute writes it into the found variable's payload at CVariable +0x1C, or passes it to CVariables::AddVariable on a miss. Four bytes where CSetFlagCommand has a bool, which is the only layout difference between the two classes.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's `value` case is `lea edi,[esi+0x60]` at 0x1534B9 then ParseFixedPoint, whose own entry says it writes thousandths through a register argument. Execute reads the full dword at 0x1532CD and stores it as a dword at 0x153303.

struct_fields.name: date
struct_fields.comment: When the change happens, in hours on g_CCurrentGameState's tick scale (+0xBDC) - the same scale and the same 43,800,000-hour epoch as CDiplomaticAction::date. The constructor (0x1F4550) initialises it from [0x170C2B8], the engine's null date. It is what CHistoryContainer::AddEntry (0x1F4660) sorts the list by and what ApplyRange (0x1F47C0) compares against its two bounds.
struct_fields.evidence: Four independent witnesses to the same offset: the constructor writes it from the null-date global, AddEntry's recorded comment calls `entry+8` the date, ApplyRange tests it against the range, and CSetFlagCommand::Execute stamps it from the tick at 0x152DEA, as CCountry::ChangeNeutrality and CFaction::AddCountry already do with their own entries.

struct_fields.name: country
struct_fields.comment: The country the change applies to, taken from the constructor's one argument (0x1EEA40, the store at 0x1EEA5E). Every derived Apply starts from it: the flag changes hand it to CCountry::GetFlags (0xCCD30) to reach CCountry +0x180.
struct_fields.evidence: Written at 0x1EEA5E by the base constructor from its stack argument, which both flag-change constructors pass the CCountry* to; read at 0x1EF273 and 0x1EF3A3 as the receiver of CCountry::GetFlags, whose body is `lea eax,[ecx+0x180]; ret`.

struct_fields.name: flag_name
struct_fields.comment: The flag to set. Filled either by CountryFlagChange_SetName (0x1EF360) from CSetFlagCommand's `flagType`, or by the history loader. SaveContents writes it as the value of `set_country_flag` (token 0x37D) and Apply passes its c_str to CFlags_SetFlag. +0x10 plus 0x1C is 0x2C, which is the whole object.
struct_fields.evidence: Three readers and one writer, all read off the bytes: the setter assigns to +0x10 (0x1EF36C), SaveContents hands `this+0x10` to the string writer (0x1EF2CB), Apply takes its c_str (0x1EF265), and the constructor runs a string constructor on `this+0x10` (0x1EF23F).

struct_fields.name: flag_name
struct_fields.comment: The flag to clear, the mirror of CAddCountryFlagChange's. SaveContents writes it as the value of `clr_country_flag` (token 0x37E).
struct_fields.evidence: Constructed at 0x1EF30F, assigned at 0x1EF36C by the shared setter, read at 0x1EF3FB by SaveContents and at 0x1EF395 by Apply.

struct_fields.name: unit
struct_fields.comment:
**The brigade being lent or reclaimed, held as a 0x28-byte by-value `CRef<CUnit>` spanning +0x2C to +0x53** - cached pointer at +0x2C, persistent type at +0x30, persistent id at +0x34, name at +0x38. Not a pointer at +0x2C, which is what the two-instruction look of GetClaimType next door invites.

**Three writers, and none of them is reachable from script**: LoadKey's `unit` case (token 0x256, 0x63B317), the copy constructor at 0x6394E0, and the two-tag constructor at 0x639260 - which zeroes it, taking +0x30 and +0x34 from the shared null-CRef statics [0x1A8CC94]/[0x1A8CC98] that nothing in `.text` ever writes. Lua registers GetUnit and no setter. The consequence is decided by slot 13: IsValid (0x63AD90) resolves this ref and returns false when it misses, so a script-built action is dropped before Apply runs.
struct_fields.evidence: GetUnit (0x63B380) copies +0x2C/+0x30/+0x34 and the string at +0x38 out as one value, which gives both the extent and the layout; luabind types its return `CRef<CUnit>`. The writers are the three `.text` writers of the class's vftable plus LoadKey's one case, and the `.text` reference scan over the two globals - 175 and 161 occurrences, no writes, with a positive control on 0x1A89790 finding 1,928 - is what makes the zeroing permanent. What would show it wrong: a fourth writer reaching +0x2C through a register a fieldchain scan attributes elsewhere, or a persistent object registered under type 0 and id 0, which would make the null ref resolve.

slots_noted: Three bodies deliberately left unnamed. Command slot 14 at 0x1530C0 (`return this->country.id (+0x40) != 0`, three instructions) sits in CSetFlagCommand, CSetVariableCommand and CSetCountryControllerCommand - one family by layout but not by any RTTI base - so it is described in CSetFlagCommand::Execute's comment instead of named. Command slot 0 at 0x153190 is shared with CCgmAlignmentChangeCommand the same way. And CHistoryContainer slot 6/7 (0x1F4660/0x1F4830) are held by six tables, all of them the CHistoryContainer family - inheritance, not a fold - and both are already recorded under the base, so nothing was added for CCountryHistory.
